input: Get a professional posture assessment from a physio

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A posture assessment can range from a quick general screen to a full-body biomechanical analysis targeting specific complaints — knowing the scope shapes which type of physio or session to book.
Whether this is for the user themselves, a child, or someone else affects who needs to attend and what kind of practitioner is appropriate.
The reason behind seeking an assessment (pain, desk job, sport, prevention) determines what to tell the physio and what kind of practice to target.
Budget and insurance coverage determine whether to use a private clinic, a bulk-billing provider, or an employer-funded scheme.
Whether the user already has a preferred physio or needs to find one changes the immediate next step entirely.
Some people want an in-person hands-on assessment; others are open to telehealth or a gym-based movement screen — this affects which providers are suitable.
Knowing what the user wants to walk away with (a written report, a corrective exercise plan, a referral, or just verbal feedback) determines what to ask the physio for when booking.

gold.taskTitle: Get a professional posture assessment from a physio
gold.taskDescription: Book and attend a physiotherapist appointment to receive a formal posture assessment.

questions.title: Which part of your body or posture concerns you most?
questions.description: Identify whether the assessment should focus on a specific area (e.g. neck, lower back, full spine) or cover the whole body, so the right type of session can be booked.

questions.title: Who is this assessment for — you or someone else?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is booking for themselves, a child, or another person, as this affects which practitioner and clinic type is appropriate.

questions.title: What is driving this — pain, a desk job, sport, or prevention?
questions.description: Understand the underlying reason for seeking the assessment so the physio can be briefed correctly and the right clinic specialism can be targeted.

questions.title: Do you have health insurance or a budget limit for this?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is paying out of pocket, using private health cover, or needs a low-cost option, which directly affects which providers to shortlist.

questions.title: Do you already have a physio, or do you need to find one?
questions.description: Find out whether the immediate next step is booking a known provider or researching and selecting a new one.

questions.title: Do you need this to be in-person or is telehealth acceptable?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred format of the assessment, as hands-on in-person assessments and telehealth movement screens require very different providers and preparation.

questions.title: What do you want to leave the appointment with?
questions.description: Establish the expected output — verbal feedback, a written posture report, a corrective exercise programme, or a referral — so the user can request this when booking.
